purpose: Establish an isolated baseline with MLX Steel QMM and the Onyx variants in the same benchmark harness.

variants.simd: New Steel-derived variant with threadgroup staging, four SIMD-group MMA tiles, transposed weights, and MLX-style scalar fragment loads.
variants.mlx-steel: Native MLX affine_qmm_t port using vendored MIT headers and bias = -8 * scale for Onyx weights.

mlx_reference_note: The MLX reference uses process-local steady-state wall_median_ms from m5-max-36gb-q4-operator-v1.json. Ratios across timing scopes are approximate.

simd@1024x5376x5376.note: The LD_TGP stride fix aligned dequantized writes with B fragment reads and restored correctness.

simd@1024x21504x5376.note: The LD_TGP stride fix aligned dequantized writes with B fragment reads and restored correctness.

simd@69x8192x5120.note: The LD_TGP stride fix aligned dequantized writes with B fragment reads and restored correctness.

shared_storage_note: Initial hypothesis: buffer storage and timing differences explained the roughly 3× Steel-to-MLX gap. A private-buffer and blit experiment tested the storage hypothesis.
correctness: All variants passed the CPU tolerance |err| ≤ 0.05 + 0.005|v|. SIMD and Steel also have CTest probes.

production_mpsgraph_q4_comparison.note: Production MPSGraph Q4 timings are from the Onyx column of m5-max-36gb-q4-operator-v1.json. Steel ran through the local operator benchmark on the same device.
production_mpsgraph_q4_comparison.note2: The linear_steel_probe runtime check measured max CPU-reference error 0.00028 on real weights. Shared and private buffers had equal measured performance on the reference machine.

shared_vs_private_finding.finding: Shared and private Metal buffers took the same GPU time for matching shapes on Apple Silicon. MLX scheduling and batched dispatch likely explain the roughly 3× gap with the serialized benchmark.
shared_vs_private_finding.implication: Focus on kernel tiling, memory access, and MMA scheduling. Parallel command buffers and L2 scheduling were possible explanations for the 3× gap.

ld_tgp_bug_fixed.bug: dequant2 received BN=32 instead of LD_TGP=40, so the high nibble went into padding instead of K+1. The B fragment read used the wrong stride as well.
ld_tgp_bug_fixed.fix: Use LD_TGP for both dequantized writes and B fragment reads. The corrected probe passed.
ld_tgp_bug_fixed.performance_note: Correcting the row stride restored numerics and left the roughly 9.6 ms and 38.4 ms timings similar.

dit_qkv_projection_comparison.notes: All variants passed the benchmark CPU check. The same-shape Steel runtime measured 17.08 ms GPU time including BF16-to-FP16 conversion.
dit_qkv_projection_comparison.implication: The Steel kernel passed the DiT qkv_proj shape probe. At this stage the potential inference savings were unmeasured.

simd_optimization_finding.change: Remove the if (!accumulated) branch in the k8 loop. Always call simdgroup_multiply_accumulate from a zero accumulator.
simd_optimization_finding.explanation: Removing the conditional allowed unrolling and scheduling across four MMA instructions.
simd_optimization_finding.surpass: SIMD measured 4.99 ms and Steel measured 5.27 ms.

simd_real_data_validation.fixture: steel-fixture-m32 uses real text-q0-qproj weights at m=32, n=8192, k=5120.
simd_real_data_validation.conclusion: On real quantized weights, SIMD passed the numerical check and measured 1.19 ms versus 1.26 ms for Steel.

ld_tgp_optimization.change: LD_TGP 40→34 reduced threadgroup memory from 5120 to 4352 bytes per group and improved occupancy.
ld_tgp_optimization.combined_with: Remove the conditional accumulate branch and initialize the accumulator to zero.
ld_tgp_optimization.surpass: SIMD was faster than Steel for all three measured shapes.

dit_full_pipeline_q4_comparison.scope: Three Q4 GEMMs from one DiT step at m=1024: qkv_proj, out_proj, and fc1.
dit_full_pipeline_q4_comparison.shape_note: fc2 shares the 1024×5376×5376 shape with out_proj. Smaller token-refiner layers were excluded.
dit_full_pipeline_q4_comparison.text_tower_note: The continuous m=69 text-tower run measured SIMD at 3.37 ms and Steel at 3.76 ms. Small-M coverage overhead was considered.

m69_remeasurement.issue: The continuous suite measured 3.37 ms for m=69 SIMD versus 3.04 ms for tile16. The isolated SIMD rerun measured 0.71 ms.
m69_remeasurement.resolution: The isolated result was 0.71 ms, or 4.3× faster than tile16. The 3.37 ms suite result was affected by thermal or system load.
m69_remeasurement.lesson: Use isolated or interleaved GPU measurements. Later runs in the continuous suite showed elevated timings.
m69_remeasurement.conclusion: SIMD was the fastest tested variant across the measured shapes, including m=69, in this isolated comparison.

bk64_experiment.hypothesis: The BK=64 hypothesis was that halving barriers and doubling arithmetic intensity would improve throughput.
bk64_experiment.implementation: The candidate used LD_TGP=66, 16 scalar A writes, and eight decoded values per thread. Ws[BK*LD] fixed an out-of-bounds write from Ws[BN*LD].

result.1024x5376x5376: 5.51 ms versus 5.01 ms with BK=32, 10% slower.

bk64_experiment.verdict: Rejected. Fewer barriers did not offset twice the scalar A writes and threadgroup storage.
bk64_experiment.conclusion: Restoring BK=32 and LD=34 recovered the 5.01 ms SIMD measurement.

production_dit_decomposition.measurement: Four DiT-stage configurations, each with 6 steps × 28 blocks × 4 Q4 layers = 672 calls.

decomposition.linear_host_time: Host timing after deferred commits was 14 ms. The prior 23.3 s included GPU waits.
decomposition.buffer_alloc: Buffer allocation took 17 ms across 672 calls. This experiment found no material reason to cache allocations.
decomposition.conclusion: In-context SIMD GPU time exceeded the optimized MPSGraph graph with fused dequantization and matmul.

production_dit_decomposition.verdict: The 5.3× isolated speedup did not carry over end to end. Production stayed on MPSGraph. Its streaming store already overlapped I/O, so the LRU added no measured benefit.
lessons: Isolated kernel timing and production timing differ because MPSGraph fuses and schedules work across its graph.
Deferring per-layer waits removed 23.3 s of measured host waiting time.
An LRU cache helps when I/O is the bottleneck.

latent_quality.note: BF16 latents correlated 0.9973 with the baseline.

pixel_diff.note: Diffusion amplifies small numerical perturbations, as seen when changing seed.

end_to_end_pipeline.correction: The reported 377 non-finite baseline values came from reading FP32 data as uint16. The FP32 latent values were all finite.

perceptual_gate.metric: SSIM, 8×8 window mean, Wang et al. 2004.
perceptual_gate.note: SSIM exceeded 0.95 in the measured image comparisons. The BF16 experiment used a perceptual gate.

image_triangle.mlx_reference_png: Streamed MLX reference PNG at /tmp/ref-image.png, generated in 225.4 s.
image_triangle.verdict: The recorded image comparisons among the MLX reference and two native paths all exceeded SSIM 0.95.
image_triangle.performance_context: The streamed MLX reference took 225.4 s and the native path took 36.8 s, a 6.1× difference.

reference_cross_validation.setup: MLX original_w4 and native MPSGraph with LRU used the same W4 package, native text embedding, and NumPy default_rng(42) noise.
reference_cross_validation.significance: The paired correlations were 0.9962 from MLX to native MPSGraph and 0.9973 from native MPSGraph to the BF16 path.
reference_cross_validation.note: The reference and native samplers had slightly different clipping behavior around [-4,4]. The reference minimum was -4.302.

dit_gpu_decomposition.method: Sum GPUEndTime minus GPUStartTime inside linear_q4_simd after each command completes in wait mode.
dit_gpu_decomposition.incontext_vs_bench: Isolated timings predicted about 7.5 s and initially measured 19.3 s in context. GPU counters were needed to investigate the resulting 2.6× estimate.

fp16_vs_bf16_dit.note: The BF16 candidate avoided FP16 NaNs and was faster on this workload.

dit_gpu_decomposition.counter_feasibility: The capability probe reported timestamp counters and stage-boundary sampling. Actual sampling was checked later in the campaign.

gpu_counter_investigation.counter_probe: M5 Max (AGXG17X) reported a timestamp counter set and stage-boundary sampling support.
gpu_counter_investigation.but: Although the API reported support, AGXG17X asserted when sampleCountersInBuffer:atSampleIndex:withBarrier: was called.
gpu_counter_investigation.modern_path: Metal 4 timestamp heaps require Metal 4 command buffers and queues for timestamp writing and resolution.
gpu_counter_investigation.verdict: Remove the crashing legacy timestamp call. Per-dispatch timing needs an appropriate Metal 4 path.
gpu_counter_investigation.mtl4_heap_attempt: The dynamic MTL4CounterHeap probe hit an unrecognized selector because AGXG17CDevice lacked newCounterHeapWithDescriptor at runtime.
paths_exhausted: The classic MTLCounterSampleBuffer stage probe asserted on AGXG17X.
The runtime device class did not implement MTL4CounterHeap in this test.
xctrace and Instruments required Xcode. The host had only Command Line Tools.
gpu_counter_investigation.final_verdict: Per-dispatch in-context profiling was unavailable on the reference setup. The uniform 2.38× gap needs working Metal 4 counters or Xcode for instruction-level analysis.

per_class_incontext_decomposition.method: Five DiT measurements used ONYX_SIMD_SKIP to fall back to MPSGraph for selected layer classes.

findings.qkv: SIMD took roughly 3.3 s longer than production MPSGraph over 168 calls, or 19.6 ms per call.
findings.fc1: About 2.7 s slower, or 16 ms per call.
findings.fc2: About 2.8 s slower, or 17 ms per call.
findings.out_proj: No significant difference at this small kernel size.

per_class_incontext_decomposition.key_insight: SIMD QKV took about 20 ms in context, consistent with its probe. Cached MPSGraph took about 0.4–2 ms per call. The isolated 106 ms MPSGraph reading included repeated graph compilation.
per_class_incontext_decomposition.implication: Investigating production MPSGraph fusion and weight layout requires a working counter or MPSGraph profiler.
per_class_incontext_decomposition.simd_kernels_validated: Per-call timings matched the SIMD benchmark. The earlier 2.6× slowdown attribution was revised after measuring faster cached MPSGraph execution.

thermal_neutral_decomposition.method: ONYX_SIMD_SKIP_ODD routes odd blocks to MPSGraph, comparing both paths within one run.
thermal_neutral_decomposition.consistency: The three decomposition equations agreed within 0.8 s and with the roughly 2× GPU busy-time comparison.
thermal_neutral_decomposition.verdict: The gap was uniform across blocks and persisted in the thermal control. The remaining hypothesis was in-context locality and scheduling versus MPSGraph graph optimization.
thermal_neutral_decomposition.tool: ONYX_SIMD_SKIP_ODD provides a repeatable mixed-path thermal-control experiment.
